title: HOLD-LC-001 rsp2 binary-table segment index and selection ambiguity envelope
question: What exact response-history segment structure and candidate-neutral selection alternatives are available before a source-owned validity/interpolation and timing-uncertainty rule is admitted?
decision_scope: T0 finite response-history provenance and selection-index intake only; no response coefficient, calibration law, likelihood, covariance, score, candidate, prediction or physical inference
method: Preserve the existing T-054 forward, T-059/T-061 observation-first inverse, owner order and promotion firewalls.
Reuse the hash-pinned response-history parent manifest and verify both local products byte-for-byte.
Parse the independent FITS binary-table layouts, read EBOUNDS and scalar matrix energy rows, and validate P-descriptor bounds without following any response heap coefficient.
Apply the preregistered covering, nearest and center-bracket rules to relative offsets -30, -15, 0, 15 and 30 seconds from TRIGTIME; retain every alternative and select none.
Run primary, non-importing independent, hostile, integrated and Lean checks; issue no intermediate PDF.
finding: Both hash-pinned rsp2 products contain one 128-row EBOUNDS table and eight ordered response segments with 140 matrix rows each. All scalar energy intervals are monotone and all variable-array descriptors are nonempty and heap-bounded. The fixed query grid has explicit covering, nearest and linear center-bracket alternatives; no production response or score is selected.
decision_reason: The existing response-history audit stopped at FITS headers and table declarations. This additive binary-table index is the next nonredundant provenance step: it resolves segment intervals and descriptor integrity while preserving the no-matrix-value and no-scoring boundary.
boundary: The index is finite metadata only. It does not admit response coefficients, calibration validity/interpolation, detector-to-geocenter timing, uncertainty, likelihood, covariance, nuisance, F_reg/F_lim/F_eff/F_obs, candidate scoring, prospective credit, microscopic dynamics, physical sector, Pre-A, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, continuum or mass gap.
evidence_level: T0 exact public-product bytes plus binary-table structure and selection-ambiguity metadata
assumptions: The parent response-history manifest remains authoritative for exact product identity, locators, byte lengths and SHA-256 values.
The FITS scalar/table declarations and P-descriptors can be read with the declared big-endian layout without interpreting response coefficients.
The fixed query grid exposes reproducibility alternatives only and is not fitted or used to tune a candidate.
The existing T-054 forward and T-059/T-061 inverse methods, owner order and promotion firewalls remain controlling.
missing_assumptions: A source-owned response-validity/interpolation rule tied to event and spectral-history windows.
A detector-to-geocenter propagation conversion with uncertainty and a common time standard.
Frozen detector, energy, background and temporal windows with source-owned selection semantics.
A joint timing likelihood or shared/component covariance with calibration and intrinsic-emission nuisance terms.
A complete candidate-neutral F_reg/F_lim/F_eff/F_obs map, immutable scorer and prospective holdout.
next_action: Request and hash-pin the owner validity/interpolation and timing-uncertainty rules. Keep the three selection alternatives, response coefficients and candidate scoring locked; do not treat the index as an event-level likelihood or physical result.
stop_or_redesign: If the parent bytes or table layout drift, stop and refresh the versioned manifest rather than silently replacing evidence.
If the owner cannot supply validity/interpolation and uncertainty fields, retain this finite index and park event-free scoring.
If a later owner changes the response contract, issue a new versioned contract; do not mutate this record or the established methods.

adversarial_review.check: Could an altered response product be accepted under the old manifest?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by exact hash and byte-length checks.

adversarial_review.check: Could numbering, interval order, energy monotonicity or descriptor bounds be corrupted?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by primary/independent checks and hostile mutations.

adversarial_review.check: Could matrix coefficients be silently read or interpreted?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by explicit matrix_coefficients_read=false and heap-not-interpreted firewall.

adversarial_review.check: Could one response alternative be promoted to a production choice?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by NONE_SELECTED, retained alternatives and hostile mutation.

adversarial_review.check: Could the fixed query grid or response choice earn prospective credit?
Could finite response metadata be promoted to microscopic dynamics or Yang--Mills evidence?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD-REJECTED; the physical owner, map and all promotion fields remain unadmitted.

adversarial_review.check: Could this additive index replace T-054/T-059/T-061?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED; methods and owner order are explicitly unchanged.

adversarial_review.check: Could a single parser hide a binary-layout error?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED; a non-importing standard-library parser agrees on the core digest.
